reviews.author: YennaPPa (Luscious.K)
reviews.text:
"Since 1981: Complete Class"

I first experienced Hanuri in 1992, so I have been a regular for 32 years.
My parents liked it, I like it, and it's one of the few family restaurants in Gangnam that my kids also like.
As you can see from Hanuri's reviews, I myself have consistently observed the history of this house and used it.
Just as I grow older and become a member of society, I feel like this restaurant has matured and is standing strong as a pillar of dining in the Gangnam area.

The rotisserie side dish, which shows the original class, has a vivid color and tastes different from the competitors right next to it.
In particular, the tangy sauce and fresh vegetables with all the bitterness removed are always a regular starting member.

You may wonder why you would pay such a high price for shabu-shabu that you can eat at home, but it certainly completes Hanuri style, from the broth to the ingredients, the taste of the sauce, and most importantly, the side dishes, and the lady's friendly service makes it an even more enjoyable experience.

The course that should never be missed is noodles, and just as pretty and handsome people know that their appearance is outstanding, this restaurant knows that their noodles are really delicious.
The noodles, which are sticky yet soft and do not spread even when boiled for a long time, are enough to create the formula “Hanwoori = noodle casserole.”

Hanuri is still the same even after a long time.
I am always satisfied with restaurants that provide complete service.

PS: The bossam kimchi they serve as a regular is still good haha.

The most delicious thing was the pumpkin pancake.

reviews.text: The beginning of Korea's first Suwon Galbi, 'Hwachunok' boasts 80 years of history. If you want to introduce the ‘real original’ of K-BBQ to foreigners, this is definitely the place. If I had a lot of money, I would come here every day.. Even Koreans fall in love with this taste, so I wonder how much foreigners will like it!!! The salt-based seasoned ribs, not an overly sweet seasoning, explode with the natural flavor of the meat and melt in your mouth (yaaaaaah). I think this is the best place to experience the taste and style of Korea on a different level, with the staff not only cooking the food themselves, but also the friendly service and luxurious atmosphere. There were many Koreans who came with foreigners, and I think that in a place like this, foreigners would be able to go back to their home countries with a good impression of Korea.

After a long time, I went to Mukjeon in Sinsa-dong with my senior on a gourmet trip.
My senior said that the only restaurant he would recommend near his house is Mukjeon.
Mukjeon is located in Apgujeong Cafe Alley behind Dosan Park.
It will take about 6 minutes from Exit 5 of Apgujeong Rode Station. Apgujeong Station is a bit far.

Valet parking is available, so a valet will come out when you arrive in front of the store.
For the Hojok class, every Monday is a regular holiday.
Open every day at 11:30 am and open until midnight. Saturdays and Sundays until 10 p.m.
Open without break times and last order is until 1:30.

Mukjeon has been in business here for quite some time.
It is a fairly large restaurant with restaurants spanning from the first basement floor to the third floor above ground.
I understand that they divide the floors by age group.
We went up to the 3rd floor and there were a lot of people around our age.

First, Mukjeon's best herbal medicine, Doma Bossam (39,000 won), was better.
The kimchi to go with the clean-tasting Bossam is also quite delicious.
Next came the seasoned scallops, which felt like I was eating them with seasoning.
I ordered water parsley pancake from Jjim's menu and it was faithful to the basics.

The kimchi stew I ordered as the last dish was disappointing.
First of all, the pork is sliced, not chunked.
In fact, it was different from what I normally eat and seemed to smell a bit.
Kimchi stew is not recommended. Haha

I heard that kalguksu is also delicious, so I ordered seafood kalguksu, which is my favorite.
I was so full that I couldn't eat it all, but noodles and soup are my favorites.
It's a restaurant so delicious that you can come here for a noodle trip.
I think I might be noticed if I go there just to eat kalguksu.

And I highly recommend the cabbage pancake. I've eaten at many places that specialize in pancakes, but the mukjeon was the best.

reviews.author: Because he’s a genius
reviews.text:
This is a place I visit often, not because it’s incredibly delicious, but because it’s easy to use.
Parking and corkage are both relatively easy in the middle of Gangnam, and the entire store doesn't have the stiff atmosphere typical of Korean restaurants, so it's good to stop by for a second taste before heading out for a drink.
However, the hall table is narrower than expected.
If you are planning to order several things and include wine, it is better to say in advance, “I will be ordering a lot, so please give me a room.”

The representative menu item, fish belly tray, has a high level of satisfaction compared to the price.
The broth, which is clear and not boiled like duck broth, is surprisingly powerful.
At first, I thought, “Isn’t the soup too transparent?” I would like to, but each bite of beef tongue and beef tongue adds to the light savory taste.
Although I don't prefer meat that has been drowned in water, this restaurant's meat is fresh and well prepared, so the drawbacks of 'meat in soup' are less severe.
The vegetable composition is simple, consisting of cabbage and crown crown, but it is well balanced with the broth, making me think, “Even if more vegetables had been added, the taste would have been distributed.”

The mung bean pancake I ordered on the side was similar to the Bindaetteok at Gwangjang Market.
It tastes a bit like oil because it's fried until golden brown, but pairing it with beer takes more effort than you might think.

Cold-je meat is as delicious as eating pig's feet or pork belly left in the refrigerator overnight.
There is no fishy or foul smell left, but it is not at the level of “completely suppressing the smell.”

The dumplings are typical North Korean-style smooth flour-skinned dumplings.
Honestly, there is no point in making it expensive.
It is difficult to say for sure that it is ‘definitely better than bibigo Wanggyoja.’

Instead, the specialty of this house is Pyongyang Naengmyeon.
Thanks to the ample broth and generous noodles, the cold noodles alone are enough to fill your stomach.
The noodles do not have a strong buckwheat flavor, so it is easy for beginners, and the broth is clear and salty.
The meat aroma is weaker than that of places like Urae-ok, so if you expect an ‘explosion of meat flavor,’ you may be disappointed.
Still, it is rare to find a cold noodle restaurant that even allows corkage and provides this much broth.

In summary, Piyangok’s greatest strength is that it is “moderately delicious and very convenient.”
The corkage is open so you can bring your own wine, and the large amount of cold noodles is always enough for two people to eat in the summer.
Next time, I plan to visit Cheongganok with a similar concept and then think again about where I will make my final regular.

It is best when the meat is grilled by an expert. Additionally, I had the Yukhoe Bibimbap and it seemed like a very good choice. Soybean paste stew served! I wanted it to have truffles, but I ate it with truffle salt. Lastly, I think that for anyone who has ever tried Tungeong Korean beef, the price here is standard. Anyway, Katsu Sand is expensive. The truffle salt here is said to be from France. The service is also very good. The mindset of tailoring the cooking level, type of garnish, and serving order to suit the customer's preference stands out.

This is a place to visit when you want to eat luxurious Jeju pork.

Located on the 3rd floor of the Dosan Meat Building, it is a meat restaurant with all rooms like a premium Korean beef restaurant, and it sells pork.

Jeju pork is cross-aged through wet aging and dry aging, and the meat definitely has a chewy texture and excellent flavor.

I was worried about how expensive the pork would be since they sold it at 'street price', but pork is still pork. It doesn't come out as much as the price of beef. Of course it's not cheap haha
The food is on par with cost-effective Korean beef restaurants, but some may say that if that's the case, why eat pork instead of beef?

I ate the bone-in style pork mahok, bone-in pork belly, and raw ribs, which are popular these days, and even the skin, and they all tasted good. I like the chewy texture unique to Jeju Island pork.

It's a high-end pork restaurant, so it's nice that the staff roasts everything.

The various conditions and side dishes are all good.

reviews.text:
#Sinsa-dong #blue

"Shower with fresh seafood"

It is a local seafood restaurant that has been on the main street of Sinsa-dong for over 20 years.
I thought I should go there once, but now that I have the chance, I do.
They run courses with different prices for lunch and dinner, and since you can order a dinner course even during a lunch visit, I requested the course that costs 100,000 won.

#configuration
Salad - blood octopus - assorted seafood - wild raw fish - raw fish for snacks - grilled bulgogi - grilled fish - meal

Salad and blood octopus feel old-fashioned.
However, the octopus feels unique when eaten with seasoned chives.

The seafood platter is the highlight.
First, you will be given a natural rock oyster the size of an adult man's palm.
Natural rock oysters are a high-quality food ingredient that are harvested by hand by diving into the deep sea with a helmet.
They say you can only eat them during the season, and in the off-season they use triploid oysters...
Because the oysters are so large, each part tastes different, just like meat.
Some parts are chewy, some parts are creamy.
However, those with a weak stomach need to be careful as the texture may bother them.

The second round of live shrimp Odori is served, and the shell is cleaned and a plate is prepared.
The fresh seafood is prepared so it's easy to eat, so it's a great accompaniment to drinks.
In particular, they added uni, making it easy to eat in any combination you like, and also emphasized the premium quality.

Well-aged, sticky white fish is also provided, and sashimi is prepared to suit the time when you want stimulation in your mouth.

This is a course that is guaranteed to fill your senses of taste that has become bored with raw foods, with grilled bulgogi and grilled fish.

#service
The service is very good.
The kindness is obvious, and the food is prepared well, so you can feel comfortable while eating.
This may be the secret to a restaurant’s long run.

PS: Although it is known as #corkagefree, it has a unique corkage policy.
Those who pay corkage, be careful!

reviews.text:
Pirata, which was enjoyed on the second floor of the alley at Hakdong Intersection, can now be enjoyed again in a new space in a renovated single-family house across the street from Yeongdong High School. The tables were much wider and more spaced out than before, making it possible to dine comfortably, and the warm lighting and sophisticated interior blended perfectly with the concept of a seafood restaurant. (Giant fish dried inside!)

The real charm of this place is the owner-chef’s philosophy of being “sincere about seafood.” We use seasonal ingredients hand-picked from the fish market every morning, some are dry-aged to bring out their deep flavor, and others are served as fresh as they were produced. Seafood that is difficult to find in Seoul is cooked to naturally mariage with wine, making you feel like you are dining in a small port city in Europe.

In particular, the course meal was creative at every moment but not overdone. “Cooking as cuisine” was demonstrated by exquisitely combining French and Italian sensibilities while maximizing the natural taste of seafood. Personally, the sommelier's recommendation was accurate, and I was much more satisfied with the selection that focused on harmony with the food instead of famous wines.

If you really want to enjoy seafood and wine in Seoul, Blue Pie Pirata is no longer just an option, it's a destination. I am confident that if continuous development continues, this place will definitely become a “treasure of Seoul.”

I hope it develops into a restaurant that follows Alla Prima, Koryoriken, and Binho!!

reviews.text: Assorted raw fish (flatfish, rockfish, salmon) and assorted seafood... Yajang raw fish restaurant in the middle of Apgujeong... Alcohol and beverages are not sold, so you have to bring your own... The only cups are paper cups... See photos for menu and prices~

reviews.author: Jaehyung Lee
reviews.text: An interesting store that sells raw fish with a nostalgic feel in the middle of Gangnam. There is no menu other than raw fish and seafood, and you have to buy your own alcohol and ramen. Recommended if you want to experience an unexpected camping experience.

reviews.author: JoonHyeok Kim
reviews.text: A raw fish restaurant that only serves raw fish. The irritated tone of voice when ordering was not friendly. Two out of three people in the kitchen took my order, but they were unfriendly. The raw fish was fresh, but I lost my appetite due to the irritated customer service. The distance between seats is very close, and you can buy cup ramen, alcohol, etc. from outside.

reviews.author: Miyami
reviews.text:
It tastes exactly like flounder and salmon as I imagined. It was delicious!! You can take it out or eat it in the tent outside the store. It was even better because you could buy additional vegetables, etc., and you could bring your own drinks, alcohol, and other snacks from somewhere else.
The price is just right and the quantity is not small. Since it's raw fish, it doesn't seem like your stomach will explode, but it's enough to make you feel full. I think I would have been full if I had eaten it with alcohol. I have to stop by often whenever I want to eat raw fish~
Oh, they say there is a point system, so you can accumulate points every time you buy something. It was a strange feeling to get mileage at a raw fish restaurant...

reviews.author: rainypraha
reviews.text: A restaurant near Dosan-daero where you can enjoy Korean beef at a relatively cheap(?) price. The main menu is kneaded beef and beef tongue, but the name itself seems to be because it is just frozen Korean beef cut into round shapes. (Originally, kneading is done by kneading and grilling with seasonings such as salt, sesame oil, and pepper.) The advantage of this restaurant is that you can quickly grill and eat bite-sized round Korean beef, but if the raw meat is good, I don't know if it is better to freeze and slice it. The special beef tongue and salted ribs were delicious, and the side dishes provided were also delicious. I can't help but feel that the young male employees have not yet been properly trained, so they often forget their orders and the place is a bit messy. Is there an uproar on Instagram? Just as restaurants are full of bubbles when you go there, this place also needs to clear up some of the bubbles. I ate it without any problems.

reviews.author: BH “Jjobojobo” JO
reviews.text: I went there by making a reservation for a table. Although the price was a bit high, the quality, service, and cooking of the meat were perfect. Corkage for a bottle of wine is free, and the alcohol list is reasonably priced. Among the numerous whiskeys on display, I and my companions were each provided with an entry-level glass of whiskey. Even though it was a 12-year-old whiskey that I had never seen before, I was very surprised by its fantastic aroma and finish. I thought the whiskey I had drunk so far was really cheap (Valen 30, Royal Charlotte 30, etc.). It was a fun time and I think I will visit again.🤗

reviews.author: Kyungho Moon
reviews.text: Following Euljiro Hall, which I was very satisfied with, I visited Dosan Hall. It was a restaurant that did not disappoint. It was a meal with important friends, and I was proud that everyone was so satisfied~! You will know the taste of the meat if you come and try it. The staff were also very friendly, which impressed me. I will come back often!
